title: Per-word reading state machine (pure): tracker events in, word states out (Unit 5 logic half)
accept: Word states exactly per the pinned machine: unread → current → (accepted | helped) → done(green); the machine is driven SOLELY by the Unit 4 tracker event stream (listening-contracts types) — it contains no recognition logic, no timers, no audio.

Fixture event streams produce the exact expected word-state sequence for a sentence, including lookahead back-fill: wordAccepted(n+1) arriving while word n is current back-fills n to done and advances current to n+2 ordering as emitted by the tracker (transcribed Unit 5 acceptance).

wordAcceptedNearMiss(index) transitions identically to wordAccepted for visual state (green) while exposing the near-miss distinction to observers (for analytics word_read result and the near-miss prompt path).

wordHelped(index, tier) transitions the word to helped → done(green); helped words are indistinguishable from accepted words in the rendered-state projection (a test asserts the render-state enum for helped == accepted) while the help metadata remains available to WordHelpRecord writers.

Current-word marker: exactly one word is 'current' at any time until the last word is done; when the LAST word turns green the machine emits a story-complete signal (consumed by the reading screen for the ~400 ms handoff — the timing itself is not this ticket's).
Multi-page stories: the machine operates per-sentence/page sequence and reports page-complete boundaries so the screen can page-turn (fixture with 2 pages).
Negative: events for out-of-range or already-done indices are ignored without state corruption (tests).
pinned_design: Unit 5 pinned: word state machine per WordToken: unread → current → (accepted | helped) → done(green); driven solely by Unit 4's event stream — the screen contains no recognition logic. Helped words render identically to accepted words (Unit 1/6 ratified: no visible marker) while WordHelpRecord rows differ. Lookahead back-fill behavior is defined by Unit 4's match policy; this machine consumes the tracker's already-ordered events. Story completion: when the last word of the story turns green, listening stops and control hands to the celebration sequence after a ~400 ms beat (the beat is reading-screen's; this machine just signals completion).
notes: Pure Dart, fully headless, no Flutter dependency beyond foundation. Kept separate from the widget ticket so the trickiest Unit 5 logic is leaf-first and reusable by twister-flow (twisters reuse green-word tracking). Exposes a Riverpod-friendly immutable state snapshot.
